<!-- board: Audit recovery is complete | Release publishing is gated | 3.2 and T-Watch stay in CI -->
<!-- reconciled-from: v1.20.0 95edaffad7eddb8543b03e5f045fbfe1fff26653 -->
**Audit Recovery.** This release reconciles the fork with the current upstream T-Watch work, repairs the build/publish pipeline, hardens storage/concurrency/update paths found during the full-project audit, and includes the first measured performance pass. These notes were reconciled against the complete fork history from v1.20.0 through the current v1.20.1 development head so early post-v1.20.0 fixes are not lost.

**Fixed**
- Replaced the final stale `squachwatch.com/update` helper text with this fork's GitHub Pages update URL. Boards still running the v1.20.0 baseline require one USB/browser flash because that older firmware's Wi-Fi OTA base is hard-coded to `http://squachwatch.com/`; newer fork builds use `https://retrodroid32.github.io/SquachWatch-CYD/`.
- SquachMesh invite reliability: an invite temporarily raises BLE listening to a 99% window, then restores the normal scan share when the exchange ends. Squad members now stay present for 20 seconds without a beacon instead of 12 seconds.
- Fixed the visitor/stale-age race caused by radio-task timestamps landing a few milliseconds ahead of the UI loop; signed age checks now keep visitors and detections from disappearing and immediately reappearing.
- On T-Watch, visitor/speech-bubble rendering now correctly sits above the corner clock instead of the clock cutting through bubbles.
- T-Watch screen timeout now applies on battery even when the global POWER SAVER switch is off. USB power and an explicit NEVER timeout remain deliberate overrides, and the crown can still force the display dark.
- Restored the Theme title-bar helper and synchronized missing upstream declarations required by the T-Watch build.
- Incorporated the current upstream T-Watch behavior without removing the 3.2-inch CYD work: automatic clock setting, motion-aware AUTO SNOOZE, BLE-arrival-aware Wi-Fi wake timing, radio self-heal, two-tap RADIO RESET, haptic standby, and deep-sleep radio recovery.
- Added T-Watch STEADY POWER, ESP32 chip-temperature readout, richer battery-log radio-hearing counters, and CLOCK CHECK / XTAL measurement so deaf-radio events can be correlated with power, thermal state, radio hearing, and ESP32 crystal error.
- T-Watch now keeps the Arduino core's stock Wi-Fi driver instead of tearing it down for the slim re-init path; CYD boards retain the slim path. This avoids a reproduced ESP32-S3 failure mode where the slim re-init could leave both radios deaf.
- Ported upstream T-Watch BLE LISTEN and SLEEP CPU controls: POWER SAVER can use a 25/50/75% BLE receive window and 80/160/240 MHz while the panel sleeps, while USB keeps the historical full listen window. SquachMesh invite boosts now return to the watch-selected base listen window instead of a hard-coded 75%.
- Added adaptive Wi-Fi channel dwell so busy channels receive more of the scan sweep while quiet channels are still sampled.
- Guarded detection-type mask width and bounds-checked per-type counters so malformed/out-of-range types cannot index past the supported detection set.
- Hardened the OTA mutex path against allocation failure and removed a deprecated NimBLE service-start call.
- Firmware product/version reporting now derives from VERSION consistently instead of carrying a parallel hard-coded product version.
- Expanded the SD filename buffer, changed SD log filenames to trusted local calendar dates when a real clock is available, and kept an honest uptime fallback before time is known.
- Fixed the SD security wipe so it removes every SquachWatch log, not only the first sixteen.
- Changed the physical NVS security wipe from a secret denylist to a safe-preserve allowlist. Encounter/history namespaces and credentials/security state are no longer accidentally restored after a duress/security wipe.
- Hardened the fork's Wi-Fi OTA path to use this fork's GitHub Pages endpoint over HTTPS, including the boot-time update check's TLS path.
- Made Bingo's cross-task pending bitmap atomic, moved DEX/Regulars state mutation out of radio callback context, removed duplicate Regulars sighting work, and deferred known BLE detections through a bounded mailbox so the NimBLE host task no longer rewrites the live detection log while the UI reads it.
- Preserved the host-test/emulator semantics for the new pending-lock and DEX changes so desktop validation still exercises the same visible behavior.
- Freed the framebuffer before Wi-Fi OTA where needed so the updater has contiguous heap headroom instead of competing with the display buffer.
- Repaired the lab-tag version path so lab-* builds bypass real-release VERSION/tag equality checks.
- Fixed the flasher board list/lab publication race and T-Watch clock setup after browser installation.
- Hardened manual lab publishing so every lab run mirrors the already-deployed production Pages root before adding lab-only assets. The mirror preserves manifests, binaries, emulator assets, retained version history, zero-byte .nojekyll, and all manifest-referenced T-Watch install files.
- Development firmware identifies as `1.20.1-dev+<sha>`; only the exact v1.20.1 release identifies as `1.20.1`. The OTA comparator treats a clean release as newer than a same-version development build.
- Repaired Pages/release handoff, rollback retention, exact emulator builds, shared ESP32 artifact verification, and board-matrix coverage.
- Production Pages no longer publishes from ordinary master builds. It deploys only the exact validated `pages-site` artifact from the release/lab workflow.
- Release publication now happens last: firmware, signatures, manifests, emulator, Pages site, and final artifact validation must succeed before a real GitHub Release is exposed.
- Real release builds require `OTA_SIGNING_KEY` and verify that it matches the public key compiled into `include/ota_pubkey.h`; lab builds may remain USB-only when the secret is absent.
- Removed the known-boot-looping 3.5-inch profile from public release/picker paths while leaving its development environment in the source tree.
- Cleaned stale fork-facing OTA/release references and removed the last machine-specific COM17 assumptions from public build/flash instructions.

**Changed**
- LilyGo T-Watch S3 is now a public beta profile in the web flasher.
- The 3.2-inch CYD/ST7798 profile gained an experimental 80 MHz display build, a dedicated web manifest, public flasher option, release artifacts, and CI coverage. The normal 40 MHz profile remains available.
- Public/release firmware profiles are required to compile in CI, including the 3.2-inch normal/80 MHz variants and the T-Watch profile. The board matrix is now the source of truth used by both CI and release assembly.
- PlatformIO library versions and the XPT2046 source commit are pinned.
- The browser flasher pins ESP Web Tools 10.4.0 and esptool-js 0.6.1. They remain CDN-hosted for this release; the README documents that residual dependency rather than substituting an unreviewed local bundle.
- Official GitHub Actions were moved to current Node 24-era major versions where compatible; the Emscripten compiler remains deliberately pinned to 6.0.9.
- Release workflow permissions were tightened to least privilege: only the Pages publisher receives `pages: write` / `id-token: write`; the release builder retains only the permissions needed to publish validated release assets.
- The public Windows 3.2-inch flash helper no longer assumes a particular COM port.
- Stage 1 performance controls bound BLE/Wi-Fi mailbox work per loop with automatic catch-up under queue pressure. Detection semantics and queue capacities are unchanged; budget-limited work remains queued for the next loop.
- Stage 1 telemetry adds BLE/Wi-Fi queue depth, high-water mark, queue-full drops, average/max drain time, budget-deferral counts, and a rolling 64-frame p95/max jitter window with >50 ms frame counts. The ten-second serial report and RADIO diagnostics expose these measurements.
- Stage 2 reduces CLEAR-screen render work without changing detection processing: layout and counter text are cached, the banter-only log scan is sampled at 4 Hz, animated CLEAR rendering is capped at 30 FPS while radio/input logic continues between paints, and fully static BLACK/boring-mode frames plus sleeping T-Watch frames are retained instead of redrawn. The serial `[render]` line reports actual draws and each skip class.
- Stage 3 replaces repeated 64-row MAC+type scans in the detection hot path with a fixed 128-bucket index. BLE, Wi-Fi, deauth refreshes and deferred black-box lookups use the index; stale rows remain addressable for reactivation, ring eviction updates the index, and chronological UI/expiry scans are unchanged. The index uses fixed storage with no dynamic allocation and periodically rebuilds tombstones to bound probe growth.
- Stage 3B removes temporary BLE scan-path strings for advertised names and manufacturer data and parses 16-bit service UUID lists directly from NimBLE's existing payload vector. It preserves complete-name preference, SquachMesh multi-block handling and UUID matching order while also eliminating the previous temporary-string `c_str()` lifetime hazard.
- Stage 3C batches SD event rows in a fixed 512-byte buffer instead of opening, appending and closing the log file for every detection. Busy traffic flushes at 384 bytes and sparse traffic within one second; failed writes retain older pending rows for retry, day rotation flushes before changing filenames, and security wipes discard pending rows before deleting logs.

**Release gate**
- v1.20.1 must not be tagged/published until the repository Actions secret `OTA_SIGNING_KEY` contains the private key corresponding to the public key intentionally chosen for this fork and compiled into `include/ota_pubkey.h`.
- If the fork rotates to a new OTA signing key before release, already-flashed devices containing the old public key will require one USB reflash before they can accept future OTA images signed by the new private key.
- Master branch protection is a repository setting and must be enabled separately; this repository currently has no rulesets, and the connected GitHub integration cannot access the classic branch-protection administration endpoint.
